newsitem.title: DENMARK: QUIET DANISH BONDS DRIFT DOWN, SEEN HOLDING LEVELS.
newsitem.headline: QUIET DANISH BONDS DRIFT DOWN, SEEN HOLDING LEVELS.

text.p: Danish bond prices drifted down on Thursday in a market steered by the dollar, with the outlook unsure but levels expected to broadly hold.
"Nobody seems to know which way the market is going, but it could fall a little. It is the currency market which is the locomotive," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.11 point from the opening at 112.54, yielding 6.08 percent. The seven percent 2007 paper, due to take over as benchmark on September 1, dropped 0.10 point to 105.40, with the yield at 6.26 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 tone-setting papers was 1.47 and 1.32 billion crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future fell 0.14 point to 112.14 with 111 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.37 point to 91.43.
The crown traded at 3.8097 per mark at 1125 GMT, down a little from around 3.8087 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 57 bps.
